rules.name: Collateral Studies
rules.notes:
Collaterals are courses offered outside the Art & Art History Department that complement a student’s area of concentration. These courses strengthen the student’s interdisciplinary study of art history.
Students entering with a B.A. must take a minimum of three collateral courses. Those entering with an M.A. must take a minimum of two collateral courses. If appropriate, one collateral may be a course in studio art.
Students must consult with their primary advisor about their choice of collateral courses prior to their enrollment. Students must complete their collaterals by the end of the spring quarter of the third year.

NOTE: Courses cross-listed with ARTHIST or FILMEDIA do not fulfill this requirement.

rules.name: Distribution Requirements
rules.desc:
The department offers two distribution requirement tracks: Art History and Film & Media Studies.
The Art History track has five areas of distribution:

• 1000 BCE-13th Century

• 14th Century-17th Century

• 18th Century - Present

• Film & Media Studies

• Asian/African/Islamic/Indigenous
Students must take at least one course in each of the five distribution areas.
The Film & Media Studies track has five areas of distribution:

• Theories of Cinema

• Media Studies

• Art History

• National Cinemas (includes international)

• Form, Function, and Aesthetics
Students must take at least one course in each of the five distribution areas.
Fulfilling the distribution requirement with graduate seminars is strongly encouraged. If students have entered the Stanford program with an MA, they may transfer courses taken at the graduate level to fulfill up to two areas of the distribution requirement.
All courses must be taught by different faculty members. Students are strongly encouraged to fulfill the distribution requirement with graduate seminars taken for 5 units.

rules.name: Qualifying Exam
rules.desc:
The qualifying exam should ideally be taken by the end of winter quarter in the student’s third year of PhD study. (Students entering the program with an MA should aim to take it in the fall quarter of the third year.) The exam consists of a written and an oral component. Each portion of the exam is administered on separate days during the same week, with the written portion taking place first. Both parts of the exam are graded on a High Pass/Pass/Fail system.
To prepare for the exam, students may enroll in up to two 5-8 unit exam preparation courses (ARTHIST620), one per quarter.
If a student fails one or both parts of the exam, they are allowed to retake that portion or portions of the exam they have failed. For a detailed account of the written and oral exam format, see the Graduate Student Handbook for the Department of Art and Art History.

rules.name: Graduate Pedagogy
rules.desc: Students are required to take ARTHIST405A Graduate Pedagogy. This course is offered every other academic year,ideally taken either before or during a student’s first teaching assistantship.

rules.name: Graduate Student Teaching
rules.desc:
Students are required to complete three quarters of teaching experiences. Students can complete more than the required number of teaching quarters, given availability.
At least one teaching experience must be in a course from the following list:

• ARTHIST 1A

• ARTHIST 1B

• ARTHIST 2

• ARTHIST 3

• ARTHIST 5

• FILMEDIA 4

rules.name: Teaching Requirement
rules.desc: Teaching is core to the academic and professional training of doctoral students in our program. All students are required to complete 3 quarters of teaching experience by the end of their third year in the program regardless of their financial support. Students may teach additional quarters beyond the degree requirement as part of their professional training and financial support.

rules.name: Advancement to Candidacy
rules.desc:
At the end of the spring quarter of the second year, faculty formally review graduate students’ progress to determine whether they meet the requirements for candidacy.
To apply for candidacy, students must submit a file at the beginning of the spring quarter of their second year demonstrating that they have completed all candidacy requirements. Students entering the program with an MA are encouraged to apply earlier during the autumn quarter of their second year. All students must advance to candidacy by the spring quarter of the second year.
Candidacy requirements (as further detailed in the department’s Graduate Handbook) include:

• Completion of all language requirements

• Completion of all distribution requirements

• Completion of all collateral requirements

• Completion of 45 units of coursework
The graduate student does not become a formal candidate for the PhD degree until they have satisfied these requirements and the faculty has voted to confer candidacy. Failure to advance to candidacy may result in the student’s dismissal from the program.
Additional details on qualifying procedures can be found in the Graduate Handbook <https://artgradguide.stanford.edu/phd-programs/candidacy-phd-degree>.

rules.name: Oral Defense of the Dissertation
rules.desc:
In the Department of Art & Art History, the oral exam is a defense of the dissertation presented upon the completion of a substantial portion of the dissertation or upon completion of a pre-final draft. Students consult with their dissertation advisor and reading committee members on the timing of the defense. The department generally expects this milestone to be completed within five years of the student's admission to PhD candidacy.

The oral defense consists primarily of a presentation and critical dissertation discussion but may range, at the committee’s discretion, over a wider field. The student is expected to describe dissertation research methods and findings at some length and to answer all questions and criticisms put by members of the examining committee. At the end of the defense, the committee votes to pass or fail the student on the defense.

In the case of failure on the defense, the examiners may establish criteria for reconsidering a resubmitted dissertation. If the defense is passed, the committee may recommend changes in the dissertation manuscript before submitting it to the university as the final requirement for granting the PhD. After incorporating these changes, the student's principal advisor gives the manuscript a last review and approval.

rules.name: Dissertation Colloquium
rules.desc:
The department requires a total of three colloquia to be facilitated between the graduate student and their reading committee.
The proposal colloquium is held after the dissertation proposal is fully drafted. At this stage, the advisor and dissertation committee meet with the student to discuss and provide feedback on the proposal prior to its final approval and signing.
The first chapter colloquium is a required review of the first completed dissertation chapter. The dissertation colloquium is held on the completed or near-completed dissertation prior to submission and defense.

rules.name: Dissertation Proposal
rules.desc:
By the beginning of the autumn quarter in the fourth year, students should have identified a dissertation topic and prepared a proposal in consultation with their principal faculty advisor.
The proposal must be 12–15 pages in length, excluding the bibliography and appendix of images. Students may enroll in ARTHIST 640 (5 units) to prepare the proposal.
The student must submit the dissertation proposal directly to their dissertation reading committee for review and approval. This should happen no later than early November of the autumn quarter in the student's fourth year of study.
If the proposal is not approved, the Faculty Committee will specify the conditions for its revision, resubmission, and reconsideration.

rules.name: Dissertation
rules.desc: Students are required to submit an approved dissertation that makes an original contribution to the field of Art History. Students are expected to submit their final dissertation in the same quarter as the oral defense. The department generally expects the dissertation to be completed within five years of the student's admission to PhD candidacy. The final draft of the dissertation must be submitted to the dissertation reading committee at least four weeks before the oral defense.

rules.name: Language Requirement Overview
rules.desc:
Graduate students must demonstrate proficiency in one language relevant to their field of study. Students focusing on Western Art typically satisfy this requirement by demonstrating reading proficiency in a European language. Students focusing on Asian Art typically satisfy this requirement by demonstrating proficiency in an Asian language.
The language requirement should be satisfied by the end of the second year of study. Students entering the PhD program with an M.A. are expected to have satisfied the language requirement before admission.
The language requirement may be fulfilled by passing a reading examination administered through the Stanford Language Center or by demonstrating equivalent proficiency through Stanford language coursework, as determined by the faculty. Students who satisfy the requirement through coursework must complete the course for a letter grade (when that option is available) and submit a letter from the instructor confirming reading proficiency.

rules.name: Subplan Overview
rules.desc: Students may petition for the sub-plan designation, either on the basis of their coursework or the focus of the dissertation.
